answer.rationale: The incumbent refuses to reopen price, the contract lapses in 14 days, and the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — a full switch to the low-cost vendor would chase the 18% mandate while concentrating all delivery risk on an unproven-at-scale supplier. Onboarding the low-cost vendor as a qualified second source on a guarded volume allocation captures partial savings now, removes the single point of failure before expiry, and creates leverage for a fuller migration once the vendor proves delivery at the required 94% volume. Before committing I want to verify memory_c2 (the low-cost vendor's actual performance record behind the 'cut cost sharply' summary — including any quality, lead-time, or ramp issues that may have been compressed out) and memory_c3 (the mechanics and timeline of adding a second source for this component) since both are consolidated memories and the decision hinges on their details.
